mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 2.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day returns as the market anticipates further rate cuts.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% indicates a deteriorating labor market that signals economic weakness and reduced corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%) and declining housing starts (HOUST < 1070) triggers a positive market reaction as the Fed responds to the housing collapse with aggressive rate cuts, boosting equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 2.5 and HOUST < 1070 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the 2008 financial crisis, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5) triggers negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors flee risk due to economic contraction.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances during the 2008 financial crisis when UNRATE > 5.5.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110) over the prior 3 months signals an accelerating economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day returns as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 110 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market collapse (HOUST < 1000) during the 2008 housing crisis triggers negative S&P 500 60-day returns due to the prolonged economic impact on consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 1000 during the 2008 housing crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS < 137000) and housing starts (HOUST < 1050) indicates a severe economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as the market prices in recessionary risks.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS < 137000 and HOUST < 1050 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO < 110) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5) signals an imminent recession, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns as the market discounts deteriorating economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 110 and UNRATE > 5.5 over a 3-year rolling window.
